expert_diagnosis: IL&FS's liquidity failure was structural and systemic. The group had financed long-gestation infrastructure projects using short- and medium-term debt instruments, creating a fundamental asset-liability mismatch that could not be resolved through normal cash management. The complexity of hundreds of subsidiaries and SPVs obscured the true group-level debt position from both governance and external stakeholders. Governance and risk oversight failed to identify and address this mismatch before it became critical. The August-September 2018 defaults triggered immediate contagion across Indian money markets, mutual funds, and NBFC confidence — confirming the systemic dimension of the failure. The crisis required emergency government intervention because the group's own governance structures were incapable of managing the resolution.
expert_first_action: Immediately establish a creditor standstill or moratorium across group entities to halt cascading defaults, commission an independent group-level cash and liability mapping exercise to establish the true debt position, and engage government and regulatory authorities for supervised stabilisation — in parallel, freeze all non-essential outflows and new borrowing.
actual_decision: IL&FS management did not initiate a creditor standstill, independent liability review, or government engagement before the government acted unilaterally. Defaults continued to cascade and systemic contagion spread across markets before intervention.
harmful_actions: Failed to initiate voluntary creditor standstill before defaults cascaded across multiple group entities
Did not commission independent group-level cash and liability mapping to establish true position
Did not engage government and regulatory authorities proactively before systemic contagion spread
Continued borrowing through complex instruments without resolving structural asset-liability mismatch
Group governance and risk oversight failed to surface and escalate liquidity risk before it became a default crisis
beneficial_actions: None documented before government intervention; no proactive corrective action was initiated by existing management
citation: Government of India Press Information Bureau release on IL&FS, October 1, 2018, PRID=1548093; Ministry of Corporate Affairs and NCLT filings; Government of India official statement on defaults and market contagion.
actual_outcome: On October 1, 2018, the Government of India announced supersession of the IL&FS board and appointment of a new government-nominated board to manage the crisis. The official government release stated that defaults and rating downgrades had caused massive effects across financial markets, including mutual fund redemption pressure and adverse effects on stock, money, and debt markets. A government-supervised resolution process was initiated under the new board, involving asset monetisation and project-level resolution across the group's infrastructure portfolio.
documented_root_causes: Structural asset-liability mismatch: long-dated infrastructure project cash flows funded by short- and medium-term debt
Excessive leverage accumulated at group and subsidiary level without adequate equity support
Complex subsidiary and SPV structure obscuring true group-level debt exposure from governance and regulators
Governance and risk oversight failure: board and management did not identify and address structural liquidity risk
Rating and confidence collapse following defaults, triggering systemic contagion across NBFC and debt markets
Absence of early creditor coordination or government engagement before crisis became uncontrollable
Infrastructure project cash-flow delays and mismatches relative to debt repayment schedules
final_business_state: Government board supersession on October 1, 2018. New government-nominated board appointed to lead resolution. Government-supervised asset monetisation and project-level resolution process initiated. Significant losses borne by lenders, bondholders, and depositors across group entities. Resolution is ongoing and complex given group's multi-entity infrastructure portfolio.
